content:
tara: Heads up — vendor invoice INV-98321 arrived showing a $48,000 charge for Feb reserved capacity but included a $12,000 contra line labeled 'pilot passthrough credit'. This wasn't in the original SOW. Potential revenue schedule mismatch for March close.

miguel: Is that $12k credited to the customer invoice or netted against vendor expense?

tara: It looks like the vendor billed us $48k then applied a negative line for $12k. On our billing export it reduced AR for the customer invoice by $12k (so net customer charge dropped). Sales says the pilot amendment promised $20k in credits, but we only expected $20k total across months — the $12k looks like a separate vendor rebate.

ashley: If the customer invoice was reduced, we probably already recognized less revenue. The risk is vendor rebate being recorded as contra-revenue (reduces recognized rev) vs. as a rebate/expense (affects COGS). We need to pick consistent treatment before close.

dan: Contract amendment effective 2026-02-10. The $20k pilot credit is pro-rated across Feb/Mar per amendment language. This $12k vendor item is a different line on the vendor invoice — ops didn't route it to Sales.

miguel: Recommendation: treat vendor $12k as a vendor rebate (reduce hosting expense) rather than contra-revenue, because it's not a customer-facing credit under our commercial terms. That means reversing the contra on the customer invoice and booking a vendor credit. But need AP/AR entries and clear audit trail.

ashley: Agreed on treating as vendor rebate if we have evidence vendor intended a rebate to us (not the customer). Need vendor communication + revised invoice. For close, temp fix is: 1) reinstate customer AR for $12k (journal), 2) book vendor rebate into other income (or reduce expense) with memo linking to INV-98321. Proposed JE: 
```
DR Accounts Receivable 12,000
  CR Contra Revenue (customer credit reversal) 12,000
```
and then when vendor issues credit: 
```
DR Accounts Payable / Vendor Credit 12,000
  CR Other Income (vendor rebate) 12,000
```
This preserves revenue schedule for customer-side recognition.

tara: That JE looks good. Can you also provide proration calc for the $20k pilot credit so RevOps can update the revenue schedule?

miguel: Sure — amendment covers 60 days (Feb 10–Apr 10). For month-end periods: Feb accrual from 2/10–2/28 = 19 days -> 19/60 * 20,000 = $6,333.33; Mar full month 31/60 = $10,333.33; Apr 10/60 = $3,333.34. So revenue deferral schedule should allocate those amounts.

ashley: I'll prepare a short journal to record the deferral and monthly recognition. For Feb (to defer the full pilot credit): 
```
DR Sales & Marketing Expense (customer credits recognized) 20,000
  CR Deferred Revenue Reserve 20,000
```
Then monthly recognitions per miguel's calc.

dan: I'll get the vendor to reissue INV-98321 with a clear rebate line and confirm routing. If vendor confirms rebate to us, we can post the AP credit.

billing-bot: Notify: invoice INV-98321 flagged for manual review and hold on auto-posting. Ticket #BILL-644 created.

tara: Action items: Ashley to post temporary JE to reinstate AR and create the deferral memo; Miguel to update revenue schedule numbers; Dan to obtain vendor revised invoice and written confirmation; I'll review on Friday for close. Please add the ticket links in the JE memo.

ashley: Will post JE and attach ticket by EOD. Thanks.
